info.name: GroupSync API
info.description:
Complete API documentation for GroupSync — location-based social platform.

## Quick Setup
1. Import this collection (Postman or Apidog)
2. Set `baseUrl` to `http://localhost:3000/api/v1`
3. Run Register → Verify Email — tokens saved automatically
4. All authenticated requests use `{{accessToken}}` via collection-level Auth

## Verification ladder

Capability is bought in rungs, so friction only lands on users asking for the riskier thing.
Several endpoints return **403** until the caller has climbed far enough.

| Tier | Requirement | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | none | Browse groups and public events, view profiles |
| 1 | email verified **+ phone OTP** | Join public groups, apply, accept invites, RSVP to events |
| 2 | tier 1 + a non-empty `bio`, then **platform admin review of the group** | Create a group |
| 3 | tier 2 + verified ID (NIN / BVN / passport) | Host an event at a **physical street address** |

Climb tier 1 with `POST /auth/phone/send-otp` → `POST /auth/phone/verify`.

## Two rules worth knowing before you test

**Groups are not in Explore the moment you create them.** A new group has
`reviewStatus: "pending"` and is excluded from `GET /groups` until a platform admin approves it
via `PATCH /admin/groups/:id/review`. It still works for its organiser and members, and is still
reachable by slug — review gates discovery, not existence. A group also needs a `coverImageUrl`
to be listed. `GET /groups/:slug` returns a `publishingChecklist` to the group's admins with
everything still outstanding.

**Event venues are split by audience.** `venue_city` + `venue_state` come back as the public
`venueArea` ("Ibadan, Oyo") for everyone. `venue_address` — the exact street address — is
serialised only for active members and going/maybe RSVP holders, and is **omitted from the
payload entirely** for anyone else.

## Variables
| Variable | Description | Auto-set |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | API base URL | No |
| `accessToken` | JWT (15 min) | Yes — Verify Email / Login |
| `refreshToken` | Opaque token (30d) | Yes — Verify Email / Login |
| `userId` | Auth user UUID | Yes — Login/Register |
| `targetUserId` | Another user UUID | No — set manually |
| `groupId` | Group UUID | Yes — Create Group |
| `groupSlug` | Group slug | Yes — Create Group |
| `applicationId` | Application UUID | Yes — Apply to Group |
| `inviteLinkId` | Invite link UUID | Yes — Generate Invite |
| `inviteToken` | Invite token string | Yes — Generate Invite |
| `eventId` | Event UUID | Yes — Create Event |
| `postId` | Feed post UUID | Yes — Create Post |
| `commentId` | Comment UUID | Yes — Add Comment |

## Response Envelope
```json
{ "success": true|false, "message": "string", "data": {}|[]|null, "error": null }
```
Paginated: includes `pagination: { page, limit, total }`
Cursor-paginated (messages, DMs, notifications): includes `next_cursor` and `has_more`

**One exception**: `GET /events/:id/calendar.ics` returns a `text/calendar` file, not this
envelope — calendar clients follow the URL directly.

## Testing Google Sign-In
The server serves a harness at `http://localhost:3000/dev/google-signin` (non-production only).
It fetches a real Google ID token in the browser and posts it to `POST /auth/social`, so you can
get a working session without wiring up a client first.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Registration, login, social OAuth, token management, password flows, email verification, KYC.

Rate limit: 10 req / 15 min per IP on all /auth/* routes in production.

request.description:
Create a new account.

Side effects: email OTP queued via BullMQ. Tokens are NOT returned here — `POST /auth/verify-email` issues them.

Password rules: min 8 chars, one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit.

**Onboarding fields (all optional)**
- `city` / `state` — captured at signup so the home feed opens on the user's own city rather than a nationwide list nobody can act on. Values from `GET /reference/states`.
- `interests` — up to 30 tags, lowercased and deduplicated before storing. Values from `GET /reference/interests`.
- `phone` — stored AES-256 encrypted and never returned. Supplying it here does NOT verify it; run `POST /auth/phone/send-otp` for that.

request.description:
Authenticate with email and password.

Requires email verification — returns 403 if the account email has not been verified yet.

Account lockout: 5 consecutive failures locks account for 15 min.

request.description:
OAuth sign-in / sign-up. Returns `{ user, tokens, isNewUser }`.

**google** — the ID token is verified against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`.

**apple** — the ID token is verified against Apple's JWKS (https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys): signature, issuer and audience are all checked. Audience is matched against `APPLE_CLIENT_ID` (comma-separated — Apple issues a different `aud` per surface). If `APPLE_CLIENT_ID` is unset the endpoint returns **501**.

`display_name` is **Apple only**. Apple returns the user's name to the client on the FIRST authorisation and never again, and never inside the identity token — so the client has to forward it or the account keeps a placeholder name forever. Ignored for Google.

Flow: known `provider_id` → sign in · existing email → link the provider · otherwise create. When the provider asserts `email_verified`, `emailVerifiedAt` is set (or backfilled on an existing unverified account) — re-challenging with our own OTP would be pure friction.

**Testing Google locally**: the server serves a harness at `/dev/google-signin` (non-production only) that fetches a real ID token in the browser and posts it here.

request.description:

request.description:

request.description:
Verify email using OTP from registration or resend-verification.

On success, returns the user object and a token pair — this is the first point at which the client receives auth tokens.

Side effects: emailVerifiedAt set, OTP deleted, session created, welcome email queued.
OTP TTL: 10 min. No auth header needed.

response.name: 200 OK
400 Bad Request — Invalid/expired OTP

request.description:
Resend email verification OTP.

Always 200. Silently succeeds if already verified. Replaces previous OTP with fresh 10-min TTL.

response.name: 200 OK — Always returned

request.description:
**Tier 1 of the verification ladder.** A verified phone is required to join groups, apply, accept invites and RSVP to events.

Supplying `phone` sets or replaces the number on the account and clears any prior verification — a new number has not been proven. Omit it to re-send to the number already on file.

**Errors**
- `400` no number on the account and none supplied
- `409` the number is already verified, or already in use by another account
- `429` a code was sent less than 60 seconds ago

**Delivery**: `SMS_PROVIDER=log` (the default) writes the code to the application log instead of sending it, so the flow is exercisable before an SMS contract exists. Set `SMS_PROVIDER=termii` + `SMS_API_KEY` to send for real.

response.name: 200 OK
429 Too Many Requests

request.description:
Confirms the code from `POST /auth/phone/send-otp` and sets `users.phone_verified_at`, which unlocks tier 1.

The OTP is consumed on success. A wrong or expired code returns `400`.

response.name: 200 OK
400 Bad Request

request.description:
Submit ID document for KYC. Uses standard authenticate (NOT authenticateVerified).

document_types: nin | voters_card | passport | drivers_license
document_url: HTTPS URL of file already uploaded to S3/R2

Document URL AES-256 encrypted before storage. Nulled after KYC decision.
Returns 409 if status already pending or verified.

response.name: 202 Accepted
409 Conflict — Already pending/verified

header.description: HMAC-SHA256 of raw body using KYC_WEBHOOK_SECRET

request.description:
Internal endpoint — called by KYC provider, not client app.

Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(body, KYC_WEBHOOK_SECRET). Invalid → 401.
Idempotency: event_id cached in Redis 24hr. Duplicates silently ignored.

On approved: status=verified, document fields nulled, S3 cleanup queued, approval email sent.
On rejected: status=rejected, document fields nulled, rejection email sent.

response.name: 200 OK — Processed
401 Unauthorized — Invalid signature

request.description:
Create a group. Creator is added as `super_admin` in the same transaction.

**Requires tier 2**: email + phone verified, and a non-empty `bio` on your profile. Without those you get `403`.

**description is required** — 40-500 characters after trimming, with at least one non-whitespace character. A 60-character run of spaces is rejected.

**Rate limit**: 3 groups per user per rolling 7 days -> `429`. Counted from the groups table, not Redis, so a cache flush does not hand out a fresh allowance; soft-deleted groups still count.

**The group is created with `reviewStatus: "pending"`.** It works immediately for you and your members, but it is **hidden from Explore** until a platform admin approves it. You are notified "Under review - usually within 24 hours".

To reach Explore a group needs ALL of: `reviewStatus = approved`, a `coverImageUrl`, `isDiscoverable`, and `status = active`. `GET /groups/:slug` returns a `publishingChecklist` to the group's admins listing whatever is still outstanding.

request.description:
List and search groups. Auth optional — affects invite-only visibility.

Search: full-text via fts_vector (name, description, category, subcategory).
Distance filter: requires lat + lng + radius_km.
Distance sort: requires lat + lng.
Invite-only groups excluded unless caller is an active member.
Deleted/inactive groups always excluded.

---

**Explore publish rule.** A group is listed only when ALL of: `is_discoverable = TRUE`, `review_status = 'approved'`, `cover_image_url IS NOT NULL`, `status = 'active'`. Members always see their own groups regardless, so an organiser can find a group that is still pending review.

**Each row also carries**
- `isPublished` - the rule above, so the client need not re-derive it
- `isActiveThisMonth` - the group has a non-cancelled event starting within 30 days. This replaced the "NEW" badge: a claim about what the group is *doing*, not when it signed up. Render it as "Active this month".

request.description:
Public group profile. Auth optional.

Returns 404 if: group not found, deleted, or invite-only and caller not a member.
callerMembershipStatus included when authenticated: { isMember, role, status, joinedAt }

---

Also returns `group.isActiveThisMonth`, `group.isPublished`, `group.reviewStatus`, and - **for the group's own admins only** - a `publishingChecklist`:

```json
{
  "reviewStatus": "pending",
  "reviewMessage": "Under review - usually within 24 hours.",
  "hasCoverImage": true,
  "isDiscoverable": true,
  "isPublished": false,
  "blockers": ["Under review - usually within 24 hours."]
}
```

It is `null` for everyone else. Reviewer notes on a rejected group reach the organiser only through here.

A pending group is still reachable by slug - review gates Explore, not access.

- `lat` + `lng`: both required together if provided

request.description:
Create an event. Group `admin`/`super_admin` only.

`starts_at` must be in the future; `ends_at` must be after it. `visibility` is `public` | `private`, defaulting to `private`.

**Venue is split by audience.**

- `venue_city` + `venue_state` -> serialised back as `venueArea` ("Ibadan, Oyo"). **Public** - present on every event payload including list and `/events/near`, so a card can show a location without a second call.
- `venue_address` -> the exact street address. Serialised **only** for active members of the group and for anyone holding a `going`/`maybe` RSVP. For everyone else the field is **omitted entirely, not nulled** - a null would tell a stranger it exists but is hidden.

Setting `venue_address` requires **tier 3** (`id_verification_status = verified`) on both create and update - publishing a street address means real people show up at a real place. `403` otherwise.

Every event also returns `canSeeExactAddress` (so the client knows which of the two it got) and a `calendar` block with `.ics` and Google Calendar links.

**Notifications**: every member except you gets an in-app notification and an email (`event_created`). A `event_reminder` follows 24 hours before the start, to everyone holding a going/maybe RSVP, with the venue address included.

  "description": "Meet at the stadium gate. Bring water.",
  "venue_city": "Ibadan",

  "venue_address": "National Stadium, Liberty Road, Ibadan",

  "lng": 3.947,
  "starts_at": "2026-09-12T06:30:00.000Z",
  "ends_at": "2026-09-12T09:00:00.000Z",
  "rsvp_limit": 50,
  "visibility": "public"
}

request.description:
Cross-group event discovery — NOT scoped to the groups you belong to. This is what "Events near you" should call: every other event endpoint is scoped to a single group, so a brand-new account with no memberships had nothing to show.

Returns public, upcoming events from discoverable groups within the radius, each with distanceKm and the group name/slug/logo/category inlined so a card renders without a second call.

Excluded: private events, past events, cancelled events, events with no location, and anything in a non-discoverable (invite-only) group.

Returns the event plus the caller's own RSVP status.

Private events are members-only: a non-member gets 404 (not 403), so the existence of a group's private events is not probeable.

---

Returns `venueArea` for everyone, `venueAddress` only for members and going/maybe RSVP holders (omitted otherwise), `canSeeExactAddress`, `myRsvp`, and a `calendar` block.

A private event returns **404** (not 403) for a non-member, so its existence is not probeable.

Downloads an iCalendar file for the event.

**The only endpoint that does not return the JSON envelope** - it returns `text/calendar; charset=utf-8` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, because calendar clients follow this URL directly and would choke on JSON.

Applies exactly the same visibility rules as `GET /events/:id`: a private event returns **404** for a non-member, so the file cannot become a side door. `LOCATION` carries the exact address for those allowed to see it and the area label otherwise, so the file stays useful without leaking the street.

RFC 5545 compliant: CRLF line endings, TEXT escaping, 75-octet line folding. An event with no `ends_at` is treated as two hours long.

The equivalent Google Calendar deep link ships inline on every event payload as `calendar.google` - no request needed.

request.description:
Update event details. Requires admin or super_admin role. All fields optional.

Body fields (all optional):
- `title` (string): max 200 chars
- `description` (string)
- `location_name` (string)
- `lat` / `lng` (number): venue coordinates
- `starts_at` (ISO 8601): must be in the future
- `ends_at` (ISO 8601): must be after starts_at
- `rsvp_limit` (int | null): null removes the limit
- `status` (string): `scheduled` | `cancelled` | `completed`

---

**Venue is split by audience.**

- `venue_city` + `venue_state` -> serialised back as `venueArea` ("Ibadan, Oyo"). **Public** - present on every event payload including list and `/events/near`, so a card can show a location without a second call.
- `venue_address` -> the exact street address. Serialised **only** for active members of the group and for anyone holding a `going`/`maybe` RSVP. For everyone else the field is **omitted entirely, not nulled** - a null would tell a stranger it exists but is hidden.

Setting `venue_address` requires **tier 3** (`id_verification_status = verified`) on both create and update - publishing a street address means real people show up at a real place. `403` otherwise.

Every event also returns `canSeeExactAddress` (so the client knows which of the two it got) and a `calendar` block with `.ics` and Google Calendar links.

Changing the time or the venue notifies everyone holding a going/maybe RSVP (`event_updated`). Editing only the description does not - a typo fix is not worth a notification.

RSVP to an event. `status` is `going` | `maybe` | `not_going`.

`not_going` is the third option the UI labels **"Unavailable" / "Can't make it"**.

**Requires tier 1** (email + phone verified) - attending an event is a tier 1 capability. `403` otherwise.

**This endpoint is idempotent.** It upserts:
- same status as before -> no-op, returns the existing RSVP (**not** a 409)
- different status -> transitions it and adjusts `rsvpCount` by the delta

That exists because the client updates optimistically and disables the button the instant it is tapped. A 409 on retry - a double tap, a flaky network, a resumed request - would force the UI to roll back a button that was already correct.

If `rsvp_limit` is set and the transition is *into* `going`, the limit is checked (`422`).

item.description:
In-app notifications, the unread badge, and per-channel delivery preferences.

**Delivery** is handled by a single dispatcher across three channels - in-app (a row plus a live `notification` socket event to `user:{id}`), email (BullMQ, and only for the low-frequency types), and push (FCM).

Preference resolution is most-specific-wins: a row scoped to the group, else the account-wide row (`group_id = null`), else defaults (all channels on).

**Which types are emailed** - `message` and `dm_received` are deliberately excluded; one email per chat message is what makes a product's email unreadable. Emailable: `event_created`, `event_reminder`, `event_cancelled`, `message_reply`, `application_approved`, `application_rejected`, `group_approved`, `group_rejected`, `group_announcement`, `invite_received`.

item.name: Socket.io / Chat
item.description:
Real-time events over Socket.IO namespace `/chat`.

## How to use in Postman
1. Open any request below — the URL already includes `?token={{accessToken}}`.
2. Click **Connect**. Postman establishes the Socket.IO handshake.
3. In the **Messages** tab, enter the **Event name** (shown in each request name) and paste the JSON body as the **Message**. Click **Send**.
4. Listen for incoming events in the **Messages** panel.

## Authentication
Token is passed as a query param: `?token={{accessToken}}`. Run Login first so `accessToken` is populated.

## Server → Client events
| Event | When fired |
|-------|------------|
| `new_message` | A new group message was sent |
| `message_deleted` | A group message was soft-deleted |
| `message_pinned` | A message was pinned/unpinned |
| `reaction_added` | Emoji reaction added |
| `reaction_removed` | Emoji reaction removed |
| `typing` | Another member is typing |
| `presence_update` | A user came online / went offline |
| `chat_lock_changed` | Group chat was locked/unlocked |
| `kicked_from_group` | You were removed from a group |
| `dm_received` | Incoming DM |
| `dm_read` | Receiver read your DMs |
| `error` | Error in processing your event |

request.description:
**Event name to emit:** `join_group`

Joins the socket to the `group:{groupId}` room. Must be an active member. All subsequent `new_message`, `typing`, `reaction_added`, etc. events for this group will be received.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "group_id": "<uuid>" }
```

**Error:** If not an active member → `error` event with `{ message: "Not an active member..." }`

**Event name to emit:** `leave_group`

Leaves the `group:{groupId}` room. You will no longer receive real-time events for this group.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "group_id": "<uuid>" }
```

**Event name to emit:** `send_message`

Send a message to a group room. Rate-limited: 10 messages per 10 seconds. Blocked if chat is locked and caller is not admin/super_admin.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "group_id": "<uuid>",
  "content": "Hello!",
  "reply_to_id": "<uuid | null>"
}
```

**Broadcasts:** `new_message` event to all members in the room including sender.
**Error:** `error` event — locked chat, rate limit, non-member.

**Event name to emit:** `user_typing`

Broadcasts a `typing` event to all other members in the group room.

**Payload:**
```json
{ "group_id": "<uuid>" }
```

**Broadcasts:** `typing` → `{ user_id, group_id, display_name }` to all room members except sender.

**Event name to emit:** `heartbeat`

Refreshes the caller's presence TTL in Redis (90 s). Call every ~60 s to stay marked online.

**Payload:** `{}` (empty)

No response event. Side-effect: sets `presence:{userId}` = `1` in Redis with 90 s TTL.

**Event name to emit:** `dm_send`

Send a direct message via socket. Same business rules as `POST /dm/:userId` — shared-group check and block check both enforced.

**Payload:**
```json
{
  "receiver_id": "<uuid>",
  "content": "Hello!",
  "reply_to_id": "<uuid | null>",
  "media_url": "<url | null>"
}
```

**Emits:**
- `dm_received` → to receiver's personal room `user:{receiverId}`
- `dm_received` → echoed back to sender (for multi-device)

**Server → Client events for DM reactions:**
- `dm_reaction_added` → `{ dm_id, emoji, user_id }` emitted to both participant rooms
- `dm_reaction_removed` → `{ dm_id, emoji, user_id }` emitted to both participant rooms

**Error:** `error` event — no shared group, blocked user, empty content.

item.name: Feed (Group Timeline)
item.description:
The group timeline — an async content wall separate from real-time chat.

**Visibility rules**
- Private posts (default): active members only
- Public posts (admin toggle): visible to everyone including non-members

**Variables needed**
| Variable | Set by |
|---|---|
| `groupId` | Create Group |
| `postId` | Create Post |
| `commentId` | Add Comment |
| `commentReplyId` | Add Reply |

query.description: Post UUID — load the next page after this post

request.description:
Returns the group timeline in two sections:
- `pinned` — all pinned posts (always full set, no pagination)
- `data` — cursor-paginated non-pinned posts, newest first

**Visibility**
- Authenticated members → all posts (public + private)
- Unauthenticated / non-members → public posts only

Query params:
- `limit`: 1-50 (default 20)
- `cursor`: post UUID — returns posts created before this one

Fetch a single post by ID.

- Public posts: no auth required
- Private posts: must be an active group member

Includes author snippet, full reactions array (with user info), and a `_count.comments` for the comment badge.

Create a new feed post. At least one of `content`, `link_url`, or `media` files must be provided.

**Upload up to 4 images** via multipart `media` field (JPEG/PNG/WebP, max 5 MB each). Images are stored on Cloudinary/S3.

New posts are private (`isPublic: false`) by default. An admin can make them public via PATCH visibility.

formdata.description: Post text body (max 5000 chars). Required if no link_url or media.
HTTPS URL to embed a link preview. Required if no content or media.
Image file (JPEG/PNG/WebP, max 5 MB). Repeat this field up to 4 times for multiple images.

request.description:
Edit the text content or link URL of a post.

**Only the original author** can edit. Admins cannot edit other people's posts (they can only delete).

Provide at least one of `content` or `link_url`.

Soft-delete a post. The post is hidden but not removed from the database.

- **Author** can delete their own post
- **Group admin/super_admin** can delete any post
- Regular members cannot delete other people's posts

Toggle `isPinned` on a post. Pinned posts always appear at the top of the feed in the `pinned` array, regardless of when they were posted.

**Admin only** (super_admin or admin role).

Calling this endpoint again unpins the post (toggle behaviour).

Toggle `isPublic` on a post.

- `isPublic: false` (default) — members only
- `isPublic: true` — visible to anyone, including non-members browsing the group landing page

**Admin only** (super_admin or admin role). Use this to surface high-quality member content as a public teaser.

Add an emoji reaction to a feed post. Each user can react with the same emoji only once (returns 409 on duplicate).

Must be an active group member.
Remove an emoji reaction from a post. Returns 404 if the reaction does not exist.

List **top-level comments** on a post (where `parentId` is null). Ordered by `createdAt` ascending (oldest first, conversation order).

Each comment includes:
- `author` snippet
- `reactions` array
- `_count.replies` — number of child replies (load replies separately via GET replies)

Same visibility rules as the post: non-members only see comments on public posts.

Add a comment to a post. Must be an active group member.

To create a **threaded reply**, include `parent_id` pointing to the comment UUID. The parent must belong to the same post.

Fetch all replies to a specific comment (where `parentId = commentId`). Ordered oldest first.

Load replies lazily (on expand) to keep the initial feed payload light.
Edit the text of a comment. **Only the original author** can edit. `content` is required.

Soft-delete a comment. Replies are not deleted — they remain but the parent content is hidden.

- **Author** can delete their own comment
- **Group admin/super_admin** can delete any comment

Add an emoji reaction to a comment. Same uniqueness rules as post reactions (one emoji per user, 409 on duplicate).

Must be an active group member.
Remove an emoji reaction from a comment. Returns 404 if the reaction does not exist.
